At 0.75 seconds physical time stops at the apex immediately BEFORE contact: all four paws are airborne and a real gap remains between the open mouth and the frisbee. From 0.75 through 4.70 seconds hold one identical WORLD state. The dog does not translate, drift, descend, paddle its legs, wag its tail, turn its head, or advance the catch. The toy does not travel or spin, and the suspended motes do not fall. The dog-to-toy distance, pose and height above the same patch of grass stay constant. ONLY the camera moves. The changing bench, trees and shadow perspectives must reveal real parallax around one frozen dog, not create an illusion of the dog running in place. Natural temporary viewpoint occlusion must not change the toy's fixed pre-contact gap. At 4.70 seconds time resumes; only in the short final beat does the dog catch the toy, descend, land and continue away. Keep the opening still's fur, color, collar and realistic park materials without replacing this camera choreography with a static shot. One continuous, temporally coherent photoreal bullet-time take.
